title: Grade 7 Science — Tue, Jun 17
description: Nutrition in Plants — Day 2 of 5: Conditions for photosynthesis; stomata and roots
subject: science

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four conditions required for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The four conditions for photosynthesis are: chlorophyll, sunlight, CO₂, and water. Oxygen is a product, not a condition.

questions.question: Through which tiny pores does CO₂ enter the leaf?
questions.explanation: Stomata (singular: stoma) are tiny pores mainly on the underside of leaves through which CO₂ enters and O₂ exits.

questions.question: What are guard cells?
options: Cells that surround and control stomata opening/closing
Cells in roots that absorb water
questions.explanation: Guard cells are special bean-shaped cells that surround each stoma and control its opening and closing.

questions.question: Stomata open during the day to allow CO₂ in. They usually close at:
questions.explanation: Stomata generally open in the presence of light (daytime) for photosynthesis and close at night to reduce water loss.

questions.question: How do roots help in photosynthesis?
options: Roots absorb water from soil, which is used in photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil. This water is transported to the leaves and used as a raw material in photosynthesis.

questions.question: What is the role of water in photosynthesis?
options: It is split to release oxygen and provide hydrogen for glucose
It carries oxygen to the roots
questions.explanation: Water is split during the light reactions of photosynthesis, releasing oxygen and providing hydrogen atoms used to make glucose.

questions.question: Which part of the plant transports water from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved minerals upward from roots to stems and leaves.

questions.question: A plant is kept in a dark room for 48 hours. What happens to photosynthesis?
options: It continues at night using stored light
It switches to using O₂ instead
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires light energy. Without light, the process stops. Plants in complete darkness cannot perform photosynthesis.

questions.question: If all stomata on a leaf are blocked, what will happen to photosynthesis?
options: It will increase as the leaf retains more water
It will slow down or stop as CO₂ cannot enter
The leaf will absorb CO₂ through roots instead
questions.explanation: If stomata are blocked, CO₂ cannot enter the leaf, so photosynthesis will slow down or stop.

questions.question: The process by which water evaporates from leaves through stomata is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves (mainly through stomata). It also helps in water transport through the plant.

questions.question: Which mineral absorbed by roots is needed to make chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is a key component of chlorophyll molecules. Without adequate magnesium, leaves turn yellow (chlorosis).

questions.question: Why do plants need nitrogen (absorbed through roots)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is essential for making proteins, enzymes, and DNA. Plants absorb nitrogen as nitrates through their roots.

questions.question: A starch test (iodine test) is used to confirm photosynthesis. Iodine turns ___ in the presence of starch.
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. If a leaf has been photosynthesising, the iodine test will turn blue-black.

questions.question: Which experiment proves that CO₂ is required for photosynthesis?
options: Keeping a plant in dark and light
Covering one half of a leaf with black paper
Placing a plant in a CO₂-free atmosphere and checking for starch
questions.explanation: If a plant is placed in a CO₂-free atmosphere and no starch forms in the leaves, it proves CO₂ is essential for photosynthesis.

questions.question: What does variegation in leaves tell us about photosynthesis?
options: Photosynthesis occurs everywhere in the leaf equally
Only green parts (with chlorophyll) perform photosynthesis
questions.explanation: In variegated leaves, only the green parts (with chlorophyll) test positive for starch, proving chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis.
